_README: Per-fixture numeric tolerances for tests/parity.rs WHEN THE PROPERTY BACKEND
IS RUSTPROP -- decision D9, docs/decisions/0009-rustprop-backend.md. The
sibling file tolerances.json grades the (P,h) TableBackend; the harness reads
exactly one of the two, selected by the same `rustprop-backend` cfg that
decides which backend install_builtin_once installs. Every fixture not named
here is compared at the default 1e-9 relative / 1e-12 absolute.
WHY THIS FILE IS SHORTER THAN ITS SIBLING. tolerances.json carries 23 entries
because D1's precomputed tables sit 1e-7..1e-4 from CoolProp. rustprop IS
CoolProp 8.0.0 (a bitwise port), so that error is gone and TWELVE of those 23
entries died when D9 adopted it:
sysdesign-ex11-liquid-cooling-loop         0e0      (was 1.3e-4)
components_wave2_flash_tank                4.1e-16  (was 5.3e-8)
sysdesign-ex17-ac-expansion-valve          1.2e-16  (was 7.9e-8)
sysdesign-ex20-zeotropic-blend             1.3e-15  (was 2.9e-8)
components_wave2_ejector_oilsep            2.7e-15  (was 5.1e-8)
components_family_fluid                    4.7e-14  (was 1.4e-6)
rankine-cycle / rankine-cycle-2            7.7e-14  (was 6.4e-7)
components_family_liquid                   7.9e-14  (was 1.2e-6)
components_wave8_hydro_turbine             3.9e-13  (was 1.6e-6)
components_bsweep_valve_characteristics    4.2e-13  (was 1.6e-6)
state-tables-multifluid                    4.4e-11  (was 2.9e-6)
A THIRTEENTH ENTRY DIED AT WAVE-2 INTEGRATION, and with it the whole
`solver_floor` section:
sysdesign-ex16-moving-boundary-evaporator   4.2e-12  (was 3.7e-9)
This file was first written against a rustprop whose single-phase (P,X) flash
still used a 30-bit bisection STAND-IN for upstream's solver, which left
~8e-10 of granularity in every iterative Temperature(P,h) -- the sole reason
the `solver_floor` relaxation existed. Wave-2 R8 replaced the stand-in with
upstream's own Boost TOMS748 plus the warm-density carry and the noise floor
went with it (rustprop's own witness: median displacement from the CoolProp
wheel over 1 433 (P, caloric) goldens moved 1.77e-10 -> 2.04e-16). ex16's
Newton block now reaches the 1e-12 engine default unaided, so both its
entries were deleted. `solver_floor` is kept as an empty object: the
mechanism is real -- any future inverse property call inside a Newton block
can reintroduce it -- but it currently has no instance.
D8 predicted this and named the trap: 'an entry whose fixture passes at the
default 1e-9 makes the parity test FAIL, so adopting [the accuracy path]
requires deleting the dead entries in the same change'. Deleting them from
tolerances.json would have broken the table configuration, which is still a
supported build; a second file is how both stay honest.
Every entry below was re-measured from scratch against the corpus, and each
survivor was traced to a named mechanism with third-party evidence -- the
CoolProp 8.0.0 wheel in rustprop's tools/golden-gen/.venv, queried directly
at the fixture's own inputs. The result is the headline of this file:
NOT ONE OF THE TEN IS PORT ERROR. Nine are the Java oracle's own (P,h)
interpolation table and one is upstream CoolProp's own unconverged flash.
At every leaf that feeds them, rustprop agrees with the CoolProp 8.0.0
wheel to between 0 (bit-identical, three of the ten) and 2.1e-13, which
is four to nine orders below the gap being graded.
The dead-entry guard flagged nothing this round -- all ten fixtures still
exceed the 1e-9 default, so nothing could be deleted. What changed is that
`relative` is now measured x1.5 for every entry instead of a hand-picked
round number, and `mechanism` is a machine-checked slug rather than a letter
in a prose key. The nine oracle-table numbers are FROZEN by construction:
the golden is a committed file and rustprop reproduces the wheel at that
state to 2.2e-13 or better, so the measured gap is arithmetic on two fixed
constants. It cannot drift; if it moves, rustprop regressed.
To reproduce any `measured` value below: run
`cargo test -p frees-core --features rustprop-backend --test parity`
with the entry's `relative` deleted -- the harness prints the fixture's
worst variable, its rel, and both sides' values.
Rules for adding an entry:
* `relative` must be the *measured* error with a little headroom (this
file uses measured x1.5, to two significant figures), never a round
number chosen to make a test pass. Record what was measured in
`measured`.
* `mechanism` must name a slug defined in the `mechanisms` object below,
and the harness enforces both directions: an entry naming an unknown
slug fails, and a catalogued mechanism that no entry names fails. A
mechanism with no instance is documentation rotting in place -- which is
exactly how the retired stop-criterion mechanism survived a whole wave
after its last instance died.
* `reason` must carry the evidence for that mechanism at THIS fixture --
which variable, which leaf property call, and what the third-party
oracle says -- so a future session can tell a golden-side artifact from
a regression without redoing the investigation.
* An entry whose fixture passes at the default 1e-9 makes the parity test
FAIL. Dead tolerances do not accumulate here.

oracle-ph-table: THE GOLDEN IS NOT A COOLPROP VALUE. The Java oracle intercepts its own
property calls: props/PropertyFunctions.java line 406 asks
PhTableRegistry.lookup() before it asks CoolProp, and the registry answers
whenever the OUTPUT is one of {T, Dmass, Smass} and the INPUT PAIR is
(P, Hmass) -- from a SaturationSplitTable built at run time on a 256-point
saturation curve and a 96 x 48 (P, dh) grid, gated only at
VALIDATION_TOL = 1.0e-4 relative. Every other output and every other input
pair falls through to the native library and is bit-exact, which is why
twelve of the sibling file's entries died outright.
So a gap in one of these fixtures is the JAVA's interpolation error, and
the port is the nearer of the two to the physics. Measured directly
against CoolProp 8.0.0 at the fixtures' own inputs, the Java table is off
by up to 6.7e-6 (Water Smass) and 1.8e-6 (R134a T) on the states this
corpus actually visits.
The control group is inside props_realfluid_r134a_states itself, and it
is complete: all 42 of its variables were checked against the wheel one
for one. The 24 table-shape ones miss it by 7.8e-10..1.8e-6; all 18
non-table ones are BIT-IDENTICAL to it -- including Quality and IntEnergy
at the SAME (P, h), which the Java's TABLE_OUTPUTS set excludes by name.
The dividing line in the data is exactly the dividing line in the Java
source. (Volume at (P,h) is tainted too, but only via 1/Dmass.)
Anything derived from these by subtraction shows more than the leaf does;
each entry states its own amplification factor.
upstream-ps-flash-residual: THE GOLDEN IS A COOLPROP VALUE, AND COOLPROP DID NOT CONVERGE. Upstream's
HSU_P flash stops on a residual that is state-dependent and occasionally
coarse. At the one state in this corpus that shows it, R134a
AbstractState('HEOS','R134a').update(PSmass_INPUTS, P, S) lands on
whose OWN pressure is 1 016 593.017 994 195 8 Pa, 4.06e-9 relative from the
pressure that was asked for -- and reports hmass evaluated there. Ask the
wheel for hmass at its own converged (T, rho) and it answers
426 479.692 669 698 04; ask it through the flash and it answers
426 479.692 738 112. The two disagree by 1.60e-10 and only the first is the
enthalpy at the requested state.
rustprop returns 426 479.692 669 696 8 -- the self-consistent value, 2.9e-15
from the wheel's own (T, rho) evaluation, on a state that reproduces BOTH
inputs to ~1e-15. So the golden is reference-side here as surely as the
table entries are, just tainted by upstream rather than by the Java.
This one is not frozen, and it is the only entry that is not. A port that
is bitwise faithful to upstream would reproduce the residual and this
fixture would go to 0; rustprop's tighter flash is the reason it does not.
Either direction of travel is a real signal and both make the entry fail --
a regression widens it, a fidelity fix kills it. Do not widen it in place:
re-measure, and if it dies, delete it.
Probed across four superheated R134a states the same p-residual is 4.06e-9,
7.31e-12, 1.16e-16 and 4.37e-16, so this is a stopping criterion, not a
systematic offset -- which is why exactly one fixture in 707 shows it.

adv_cyclepath_rankine_order.reason: Turbine TU calls Entropy(Water, P = 3 MPa, h = 3.2 MJ/kg) for tu.s_in. The wheel says 6875.8853309733604 and so does rustprop, bit-identically; the golden says 6875.8942338679017, off by 1.29e-6. Enthalpy(Water, P, s) carries that into tu.h_s and the turbine work tu.w = 0.85*(h_in - h_s) amplifies it 3.6x to 4.71e-6. Reconstructing w_t from the wheel alone gives 599317.89272939134 against rustprop's 599317.89272939321 (3e-15) and the golden's 599315.07191367587 (4.71e-6) -- the whole gap is the Java table.

components_family_ac.reason: The worst variable IS the leaf, undiluted: rho_xc = XC.rho_in = Density(R134a, P = 1 MPa, h = 260 kJ/kg). The wheel says 711.62596342460279, rustprop 711.62596342460495 (3.0e-15), the golden 711.62541994688729 (7.64e-7). No amplification anywhere -- this fixture measures the Java's Dmass table directly.

components_family_twophase.reason: SEN reads Temperature(R134a, P = 900 kPa, h = 450 kJ/kg): the wheel and rustprop both give 339.69624956356972 EXACTLY, the golden gives 339.69574815743835, off by 1.48e-6. sen.tsat at the same pressure is a (P,Q) call, bit-exact on both sides, so sen.sh = T - Tsat subtracts a tabulated temperature from an exact one and the Java's 0.0005 K error lands undiluted on a 31.02 K superheat -- 1.62e-5, which is 10.9x the leaf.

components_wave2_capillary_tube.reason: ct.t_in = Temperature(R134a, P = 1.2 MPa, h = 255495.856059855229) is bit-identical between rustprop and the wheel at 312.56110907545707; the golden is 312.56089605636430, off 6.82e-7. P_sat of that temperature amplifies it 8.4x to 5.74e-6 on ct.pf (wheel 1000632.3908855298 = rustprop exactly, golden 1000626.651703218) and dp_eff = 1.2 MPa - pf amplifies 5.0x more, because the difference is a fifth of the pressures it is made of. dp_eff from the wheel alone is 199367.60911447019 against the golden's 199373.348296781885: 2.88e-5, the whole measured gap.

components_wave2_short_tube_choke.reason: Identical to components_wave2_capillary_tube down to the last digit -- same fluid, same 1.2 MPa / 255495.856 J/kg inlet, same Temperature -> P_sat -> dp_eff chain -- because the two documents share their operating point. This fixture additionally exposes the Dmass table on sta.rho_in: wheel 1150.8741626654194, rustprop 2.0e-16 away, golden 5.69e-7 away.

components_wave2_liquid_tms.reason: The cleanest demonstration in the corpus, because the true answer is known a priori and needs no oracle at all. Each LiquidSource imposes a temperature and converts it to h with Enthalpy(Water, P, T) -- bit-exact on both sides -- and each wall-HX inverts it with Temperature(Water, P, h), which the Java answers from its table. At the source that states exactly 400 K (LPin TS2, P = 300 kPa), rustprop's round trip returns 400.00000000000004 and the Java returns 400.00067812484809. Running the same round trip through the wheel alone -- Hmass(P,T) then T(P,Hmass) -- gives 399.99999999999375, so the port is if anything the closer of the two to the imposed value, and the gap is the Java's 6.8e-4 K inversion error against a round number. (Under the pre-Wave-2 bisection stand-in rustprop returned 399.99999991478 here; TOMS748 moved that to 4e-14 of the imposed value, and the fixture's measured error barely moved, because the Java's error dominates it by four orders of magnitude.)

ev-thermal-management.reason: 178x better than the same fixture on the table backend (8.95e-4), because the FRAUX1 glycol grid that dominated it is gone -- rustprop answers INCOMP::MEG exactly, so the Re = 2987 laminar/turbulent blend has nothing left to amplify. What remains is the refrigerant side: cmp.s_in = Entropy(R1234yf, P = 328298.535 Pa, h = 371316.618 J/kg). Asked at the JAVA's own inputs the wheel answers 1624.1967310135703 and the golden says 1624.1963561235248, off 2.31e-7; rustprop sits 1.3e-13 from the wheel at its own. The isentropic outlet carries it to cmp.out.h (4.45e-7) and cmp.w = h_out - h_in amplifies 22x to 5.04e-6, which cop_cool then inherits exactly.

props_realfluid_r134a_states.reason: A pure property matrix with literal inputs, so every variable can be checked against the wheel one for one -- and this is the fixture that proves the mechanism. All 42 were: the 24 table-shape ones ((P,h) -> T/Dmass/Smass) miss the wheel by 7.8e-10 to 1.7523e-6, and all 18 non-table ones, INCLUDING Quality and IntEnergy at the same (P, h), are bit-identical to it. The worst, t_h2s = Temperature(R134a, P = 1016593.022 Pa, h = 426479.692738112), is 319.4387807966298 on the wheel, 319.4387807966299 on rustprop (one ulp) and 319.43934055826605 in the golden. Golden-vs-wheel there is 1.7523e-6 -- the fixture's measured error to five figures, so rustprop contributes nothing to it. NOTE: the investigation expected this fixture to newly FAIL under an accurate backend. It does not; it lands at 0.65 of its declared band.

props_realfluid_water_states.reason: The same complete one-for-one check on water -- all 49 variables -- with the same split: the 21 table-shape ones miss the wheel by 0 to 6.7019e-6 and 27 of the 28 non-table ones are bit-identical to it. The 28th is v_2ph, tainted only because the Java reports Volume as 1/Dmass off the tabulated density. The worst is s1_rank = Entropy(Water, P = 10 kPa, h = 191805.94455889906) -- and its true value is pinned twice over, because the same document's sf_p = Entropy(Water, P = 10 kPa, x = 0) is a saturation call the Java does NOT intercept and reads 649.1956051939358, bit-exact to the wheel, while the table answers 649.1999560623602 at the enthalpy of that very state. Golden-vs-wheel 6.7019e-6, equal to the measured error.

refrigeration-vcr.reason: The only fixture in the corpus with no table shape anywhere in it -- P_sat, (T,x), (P,x) and (P,s) all fall through the Java to the native library -- so every golden here is a real CoolProp 8.0.0 value, and p1, p2, s1 and t_evap are bit-identical between the engines. The gap is at h2s = Enthalpy(R134a, P = p2, s = s1), where the wheel's flash leaves its own state 4.06e-9 in pressure from what was asked and evaluates h there: golden 426479.692738112, rustprop 426479.6926696968, and the wheel's own converged (T, rho) re-evaluated gives 426479.69266969804 -- i.e. rustprop matches the state (to 2.9e-15), the golden matches the flash (bitwise). w_c = (h2s - h1)/eta amplifies 12.6x to 2.02e-9 and cop = q_L/w_c inherits it unchanged. Previous measurement was 2.96951e-9; Wave-2's TOMS748 work moved it to 2.02e-9 by tightening rustprop's side further, which is the opposite direction from a regression.
